title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Traditional psychometrics



Traditional assessments and psychometric models measure an overall skill or ability
Assume a continuous latent trait

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Diagnostic measurement

Designed to be multidimensional
No continuum of student achievement
Categorical constructs

Usually binary (e.g., master/nonmaster, proficient/not proficient)


Several different names in the literature

Diagnostic classification models (DCMs)
Cognitive diagnostic models (CDMs)
Skills assessment models
Latent response models
Restricted latent class models

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Diagnostic psychometrics



Rather than measuring a single trait, we can break the construct into a set of skills or attributes













Attributes are categorical, often dichotomous (e.g., proficient vs. non-proficient)

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Benefits of diagnostic assessments



DCMs place individuals into skill profiles

Fine-grained feedback to inform instructional decisions (Thompson & Clark, 2024)
Group students with similar profiles
Answer more detailed questions about student achievement


High reliability with fewer items

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Utility of diagnostic results

Attribute-level feedback about student learning is more actionable for instructional decision-making (Thompson & Clark, 2024)
However, the uniqueness and complexity of DCMs can create a “black box” for practitioners and stakeholders

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
What is measr?

R package that automates the creation of Stan scripts for DCMs
Wraps rstan or cmdstanr to estimate the models

Provides transparency in how diagnostic results are reported

Probability-based score reporting
Comprehensive and intuitive reliability indices
Auditable analysis pipeline

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Data for example

Examination for the certificate of proficiency in English (ECPE; Templin & Hoffman, 2013)

28 items measuring 3 total attributes
2,922 respondents


3 attributes

Morphosyntactic rules
Cohesive rules
Lexical rules

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Model estimation with measr


Specification
Estimation



Specify a DCM with dcm_specify()

ecpe_spec <- dcm_specify(
  qmatrix = ecpe_qmatrix,
  identifier = "item_id",
  measurement_model = lcdm(),
  structural_model = unconstrained()
)



Estimate a DCM with dcm_estimate()

ecpe_lcdm <- dcm_estimate(
  dcm_spec = ecpe_spec,
  data = ecpe_data,
  identifier = "resp_id"
)

Probability-based score reporting



measr supports reporting the probability of mastery
Can be used to communicate confidence in classifications (Bradshaw & Levy, 2019)

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Evaluating classifications

Rather than individual attribute classifications, we can evaluate across the population of respondents (Johnson & Sinharay, 2018)

Accuracy: Probability the estimated classification is “correct”
Consistency: Probability that two parallel forms result in the same classification (i.e., test-retest)





measr_extract(ecpe_lcdm, "classification_reliability")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   attribute       accuracy consistency
#>   <chr>              <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 morphosyntactic    0.893       0.812
#> 2 cohesive           0.851       0.795
#> 3 lexical            0.919       0.853

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Evaluating probabilities

We can also evaluate the mastery probabilities across respondents (Johnson & Sinharay, 2020)

Informational: The proportion of uncertainty in an examinees mastery status that is eliminated by observing their item responses





measr_extract(ecpe_lcdm, "probability_reliability")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   attribute       informational
#>   <chr>                   <dbl>
#> 1 morphosyntactic         0.572
#> 2 cohesive                0.500
#> 3 lexical                 0.589

title: Open and transparent scoring with measr
text:
Evaluating scoring pipelines

Scoring algorithms are often a “black box”

measr is completely open source

Available on GitHub: https://github.com/r-dcm/measr

Examine exactly how measr estimates models and calculates evaluation metrics (e.g., model fit, reliability)


Users can also host their analysis scripts using measr, allowing other experts or the public to evaluate how the software was used
